title: Multilingual Arbitrage: Optimizing Data Pools to Accelerate Multilingual Progress

live_model.evidence: "we use a separate reward model for routing from the model that we use for our LLM-as-a-judge evaluation...(GPT-4-Turbo) given the known biases incurred by using the same model for both"

prompt.note: GPT-4-Turbo is used only as the fixed win-rate judge over the authors' own student-model outputs; no prompt specific to it is given.

claim.metric: none for the live id (win rates of 51.8% etc. describe the authors' trained student models, judged by GPT-4-Turbo, not GPT-4-Turbo's own performance)

data.source: Dolly-15k (translated), Aya, XCOPA and other public multilingual benchmarks

notes: A rich multilingual knowledge-distillation paper (teacher-routing for student training) with GPT-4-Turbo used solely as the LLM-as-a-judge for win-rate evaluation; the paper's headline numbers characterize its own student/router models, not GPT-4-Turbo.
